title: Tenant bubble isolation with priority failover and quota policing
creator: Ava Chen
description: Deliver a tenant-level isolation mechanism ("bubble") that combines lightweight resource fencing, noisy-neighbor detection, and priority-driven preemption so dedicated GPU pools can offer throughput guarantees while allowing controlled burst behavior.
proposed_design: High-level: introduce a Tenant Bubble abstraction implemented by a combination of three runtime components: (1) admission & token-bucket lease controller that enforces per-tenant sustained throughput and burst credits, (2) an online noise fingerprinting service that scores workloads by interference risk using micro-benchmarks + metrics (SM utilization, L2 evictions, PCIe stalls), and (3) a fast soft-preemption path that reclaims ephemeral lanes for higher-priority tenants and triggers graceful model fallbacks. Implementation notes: use cgroup-like isolation for scheduler-level token accounting, colocate a lightweight tenant-side agent to manage KV cache namespaces and prefix-aware cache eviction, and add a Priority Failover API that application teams can subscribe to for negotiated degraded-mode behavior (e.g., switch to smaller quantized model or shorter sequence-length profile). The design supports per-tenant QoS classes and a burst-reservoir policy tied to reserved throughput commitments.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Canary on one dedicated pool with non-prod tenants (2 weeks) to validate token accounting and metric collection. Phase 2: Add noisy-neighbor detector and automated eviction scoring, run for 3 weeks with telemetry. Phase 3: Enable soft-preemption and Priority Failover API for selected enterprise customers, monitor SLOs for 4 weeks. Phase 4: Gradual ramp to all dedicated pools with opt-out window and playbook for support.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant steady throughput guarantees respected within 95% of targets under mixed load in canary cluster
Burst credits consumed/depleted correctly and replenished per policy
Noisy-neighbor detector surfaces >80% of past incidents in retrospective tests
Priority failover triggers and fallback model endpoints are reachable within 1s of reclaim decision
End-to-end latency tail (p99) for high-QoS tenants does not regress by >10% after enabling bubbles

comments: 2025-03-03 Ava Chen: Initial ticket created after SRE workshop — goal is to avoid hard slicing while preserving committed throughput.
2025-03-05 Miguel Soto: Spike results show we can detect noisy jobs using L2 miss ratio + SM utilization; need to validate false positive rate.
2025-03-07 Priya Nair (SRE): Recommend adding short-term tenant shadowing to validate eviction impact before preemption is enabled.
2025-03-09 Design review: agreed to keep KV namespaces per tenant rather than per-job to reduce churn; follow-up on cache eviction policy required.
2025-03-10 Miguel Soto: Implemented admission controller prototype; open PR for review: see link below. Can start canary next week if PR feedback is minor.
risks: False positives from noise detector could throttle legitimate bursty workloads — mitigated with shadow mode and manual whitelist
KV namespace fragmentation increases cache miss rate — mitigated by adaptive eviction that prioritizes cross-tenant cold keys for aging
Preemption may tear down in-flight requests if not gracefully negotiated — mitigated by adding per-route graceful-fallback timeouts and client SDK hooks
Operational complexity: new telemetry and playbooks required for on-call teams
dependencies: infra: permissions for canary fleet tagging and metric retention
notes: This approach aims for a middle-ground between hard GPU carving and full multi-tenant sharing. Focus is on predictable economics for paying customers while preserving platform utilization through controlled bursts.
migration_steps: Enable tenant bubble on a small non-prod pool and mirror production traffic for two weeks
Run shadow-mode noisy-detector to produce candidate evictions (no action) and evaluate recalls
After tuning, enable soft-preemption for a subset of customers with explicit fallbacks configured
Full rollout with automated SLA checks and opt-out for legacy contracts
